styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate car reads clearly as a rusted wreck. Its measured facts are close to the references: 15 visible tones per tile against 9-20 for the hedge, stall and well, 18% near-flat coverage against 13% for the stall, and 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted (dark blue and brown-red) and not a black sticker line. Weaknesses by eye: the body panels are mostly 3-4 blue steps with few per-panel highlights. Rust is shown as scattered orange dots, not shaded patches. The roof, hood and trunk are fairly smooth with little grain. The windows and tyres are small dark masses with little internal shading. It is a bit flatter and smaller in detail than the well and the stall, which carry 5-6 steps per material with one-by-one shaded stones and cloth folds. It is above the bench and lamp on the numbers, but those are thin props where the density fact does not apply. Overall it is near the bar but not clearly equal, and with doubt this leans toward fail.
